articles.title: Text Classification Using Graph Neural Networks: A Comparative Analysis
articles.authors: Wang K; Ding Y; Han SC
articles.keywords: GNN; text classification; NLP; graph construction; node features; transfer learning
articles.abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of graph-based text representation methods combined with GNN architectures for text classification. Twelve GNN architecture variants are evaluated using 3 message-passing layers and 4 pretrained word embedding techniques. Five prominent text classification datasets spanning diverse domains and including both short and longer documents are used. The study investigates efficacy versus efficiency trade-offs, an aspect neglected in prior work. Results show that graph methods generalize variably across datasets, and that ECAP-like cropping strategies improve handling of rare and long-tail classes.

Objectives: The differential diagnosis of ameloblastoma and OKC is essential for surgical planning. DL-based methods show promise but face clinical translation challenges due to insufficient interpretability. Methods: An InceptionV3 model was evaluated on 128 pathologically confirmed CBCT scans (AME:64; OKC:64) by 5-fold cross-validation comparing four input types: original slice, bounding-box ROI, precise segmentation ROI, and moderately expanded ROI. Grad-CAM and confidence curve analysis were used for XAI. Results: Precise segmentation ROI significantly improved diagnostic accuracy and confidence at the patient level. Conclusion: Segmentation-guided preprocessing supports clinical implementation of CAD systems for ameloblastoma/OKC diagnosis.

articles.title: Differential Diagnosis of OKC and SBC on Panoramic Radiographs: Leveraging Deep Learning Algorithms
articles.authors: Park JH; Kwak EJ; et al. (Pusan National University Dental Hospital)
articles.keywords: deep learning; differentiation; diagnosis; odontogenic keratocyst; simple bone cyst; panoramic radiograph
articles.abstract: Objective: To determine if deep learning can distinguish OKC from simple bone cyst (SBC) on preoperative panoramic radiographs. Methods: Retrospective analysis of 63 OKC and 125 SBC cases (2018–2022) from Pusan National University Dental Hospital. Results: CNN-based model achieved significant discrimination between OKC and SBC despite their similar radiographic appearances, both presenting as radiolucent lesions. Conclusion: Deep learning offers a promising diagnostic tool for difficult panoramic differential diagnoses involving radiolucent jaw lesions.

articles.title: Classificação de Ameloblastoma, Cisto Periapical e Osteomielite Supurativa Crônica com Aprendizado Semissupervisionado
articles.title_en: Semi-Supervised Learning for Classification of Ameloblastoma, Periapical Cyst, and Chronic Suppurative Osteomyelitis
articles.authors: Liang B; Qin H; Nong X; et al.
articles.keywords: WaveletFusion-ViT; ameloblastoma; periapical cyst; osteomyelitis; semi-supervised learning; CBCT; panoramic; classification
articles.abstract: Este estudo propõe o modelo WaveletFusion-ViT para diagnóstico automático de lesões maxilofaciais usando imagens panorâmicas de CBCT. O modelo emprega aprendizado semissupervisionado para classificar ameloblastoma (AM), cisto periapical (PC) e osteomielite supurativa crônica (CSO), alcançando acurácia de 91,47% utilizando menos de 20% dos dados rotulados. A fusão de wavelets com Vision Transformer (ViT) permite capturar características multiescala das lesões, superando abordagens supervisionadas tradicionais mesmo com dados anotados limitados. O método tem potencial para reduzir a dependência de grandes datasets rotulados no diagnóstico por imagem odontológica.
